==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|co-operate||UK}}
* {{alt|en|coöperate||dated}}

===Etymology===
Originated 1595–1605 from {{der|en|la-lat|cooperātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la-lat|cooperor||to work with}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} for more. Equivalent to {{af|en|co-|operate}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|efnwyrċan}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/kəʊˈɒp.ə.ɹeɪt/|/kuˈɒp.ə.ɹeɪt/|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/kəˈwɔpəɹɛjt/|a=SSB}}
** {{audio|en|en-uk-cooperate.ogg|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/koʊˈɑ.pəˌɹeɪt/|/kuˈɑ.pəˌɹeɪt/|/kəˈwɑ.pəˌɹeɪt/|/-ɚˌ-/|a=US,CA|q2=rare|q3=colloquial}}
** {{audio|en|En-cooperate.ogg}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-cooperate.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/kəʉˈɔp.ə.ɹæɪt/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/kɐʉˈɒp.ə.ɹæɪt/|[kɐʉˈɔ̟p.ə.ɹæɪt]|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒpəɹeɪt|s=4}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To work or act together, especially for a common purpose or benefit.
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=November 7, 2012|author=Matt Bai|title=Winning a Second Term, Obama Will Confront Familiar Headwinds|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/07/us/politics/in-president-obamas-second-term-familiar-challenges.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0
|passage=In polling by the Pew Research Center in November 2008, fully half the respondents thought the two parties would '''cooperate''' more in the coming year, versus only 36 percent who thought the climate would grow more adversarial.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251106105818/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/07/us/politics/in-president-obamas-second-term-familiar-challenges.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0|archivedate=6 November 2025}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To allow for mutual unobstructed action.
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To function in harmony, side by side.
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To engage in economic [[cooperation]].
# {{lb|en|law|_|jargon|transitive}} To obtain the cooperation of (a potential [[witness]]); to turn (someone) into a cooperating witness.<ref>Liberman, Mark and various commenters (2024), “[https://languagelog.ldc.upenn.edu/nll/?p=64211 ‘Cooperate him’]”, in ''Language Log''.</ref>

====Usage notes====
<!-- this note sucks -->
* The usual pronunciation of 'oo' is /uː/ or /ʊ/. The [[diaeresis]] in the spelling of [[coöperate]], now archaic outside the pages of ''{{w|The New Yorker}}'', was intended to emphasize that the second ''o'' begins a separate syllable.
* The solid form is much more common than the hyphenated form in both British and American corpora. The hyphenated form was formerly more common in British usage, but is now rarely seen.<ref>{{R:GNV|cooperate,co-operate}}</ref>
